clue.text: Our side in protective gear roughly handled

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other, our side inside the protective gear

parts.note: a pad is protective gear worn by cricketers and hockey players
our side is us, the group speaking: we

explanation.surface: Our team, kitted out in its protective gear, was knocked about.
explanation.definitionFit: To paw someone is to touch or grope them clumsily, a rough kind of handling.

clue.text: After pressure I'm savage with united, wrongly giving extra penalty

indicators.note: After says the rest comes later, following pressure

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of the following words are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A football club is fined after a player's violent outburst under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges IM SAVAGE and UNITED; P goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A court awards these on top of compensation to punish the wrongdoer, an extra penalty.

clue.text: Girl with aim — matrimony at last!

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

indicators.note: at last tells us to take the final letter of matrimony

explanation.surface: A young woman whose goal is finally reached when she marries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes Y, the final letter of 'matrimony'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female first name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Daily diary one girl replaced with another

indicators.note: replaced with says the first girl's name is swapped for the second's

parts.note: a journal is a diary
Jo is a girl's name
Di is another girl's name

explanation.surface: A diary kept every day records one girlfriend replaced by another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced with' swaps JO in JOURNAL for DI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done every day, or by day rather than night, is this.

clue.text: School dunces get these for geometry

parts.note: a comp is short for a comprehensive, the British state secondary school
asses are fools or dunces

explanation.surface: Struggling pupils are handed instruments for their maths lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: A comp is a British comprehensive, a state secondary school open to all abilities.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of drawing instruments used to scribe circles is a standard piece of geometry kit.

clue.text: In church, allowed something for heating

indicators.note: In says the word for allowed goes inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OK means approved or allowed

explanation.surface: Inside a church, permission is given for fuel to warm the building.
explanation.definitionFit: This fuel made from coal is burned in furnaces and stoves to give heat.

clue.text: An old man, see me so fit, standing on head

parts.note: so in the sense of in this way means thus

indicators.note: standing on head says the word for fit is turned upside down, read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: hale means fit and healthy

explanation.surface: An elderly man shows off how well he keeps by doing a headstand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing on head' turns HALE upside down in this down clue, giving ELAH. 'see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's longest-lived patriarch, said to reach 969, is the type of a very old man.

clue.text: I don't believe tea can be brewed with this

definitions.note: the definition is what such a person would say, standing for the person

indicators.note: can be brewed says the letters of the following words are stewed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sceptical claims you cannot make tea with this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be brewed' rearranges TEA and THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who denies the existence of any god would declare a lack of faith.

clue.text: Napkins unfurled before queen, an expanse of cloth

indicators.note: unfurled says the letters of napkins are spread out into a new order

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Table napkins are shaken out before the Queen arrives, a great spread of linen.
explanation.definitionFit: This large balloon-shaped sail on a racing yacht is a big expanse of sailcloth.

clue.text: Wind through blades makes an unsuspected danger

parts.note: to wind is to twist and turn like a serpent
moving through blades of a lawn is being among its stalks

explanation.surface: A breeze passing through the lawn creates a hidden hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as a breeze, but it is the verb rhyming with 'find', meaning to twist like a serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: A treacherous person who seems a friend is the classic hidden peril, from Virgil's lurking serpent.

clue.text: Relation is to flourish in island resort

parts.note: a nan is a grandmother, a family relation
a tucket is an old word for a trumpet fanfare or flourish

explanation.surface: A relative is set to prosper at a seaside holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flourish' looks like a verb meaning thrive, but here it is the noun: a trumpet call, TUCKET in Shakespearean stage directions.
explanation.definitionFit: This island off Massachusetts, once a whaling port, is now a summer holiday destination.

clue.text: City's footballers on the road at end of match

indicators.note: on says the footballers come next, after the road
end of says we want the final letter of the word match

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, written here with the figure 1 as the letter I
the FA is the Football Association, the governing body of English football

explanation.surface: The city's football team are on the road home once the game is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's main road from London to Edinburgh; crosswords write its 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: This Israeli port on the Mediterranean is a large city.

clue.text: Upsetting work on bench

definitions.meaning: distressing or exasperating, as in a difficult day
what a judge on the bench does to a case: hearing it in court

explanation.definitionFit: Exasperating behaviour wears you down; and a judge hearing a case in court is at work on the bench.

clue.text: How veg may be prepared right in the summer

indicators.note: in says the word for right is placed inside the summer month

parts.note: June is a summer month
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A tip on cooking seasonal vegetables properly in summertime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' is not R here but a legal claim on property.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetables cut into matchstick strips are said to be done in this style, a kitchen term.

clue.text: Set up to keep new monk out of order

indicators.note: to keep says the word for set up holds the next pieces inside

parts.note: to set up is to raise, as in raised
Dom is the title of a Benedictine monk

explanation.surface: A monk is put up to keep a newcomer away from the religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' suggests a religious order, fitting the monk, but 'out of order' means jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged by chance with no fixed sequence, so jumbled and in no order.

clue.text: Be in two minds: leave? I will come in

indicators.note: come in says the I will piece enters the word for leave

parts.note: to vacate a place is to leave it
I will contracts to I'll, written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone torn over whether to quit announces they will join after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I will' contracts to I'll, and the apostrophe is ignored, as crossword convention allows.
explanation.definitionFit: To waver is to keep switching between two options, unable to settle.

clue.text: Officer to take a risk about fight, a court-martial offence

indicators.note: about says the officer and the risk-taking go round the fight

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
to dice, as in dice with death, is to take a risk
a war is a fight

explanation.surface: An officer gambles over a battle and ends up charged by a military court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the officer and the gamble together around the fight, rather than wrapping the gamble alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing fear in the face of the enemy is a military crime tried by a court-martial.

clue.text: Fell into trap, returning to counter

indicators.note: returning says the whole construction is read backwards
into says the word for fell goes inside the trap

parts.note: a net is a trap for fish or birds
to fell an opponent is to knock him out, a KO

explanation.surface: Someone tumbled into a snare and went back to the shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' builds NEKOT, and 'returning' turns that whole run round.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a disc or chip used in a game, a sense of counter.

clue.text: Actor keeps wife in a sort of house

indicators.note: keeps says the actor holds the wife inside

parts.note: an actor in the sense of one who acts is a doer

explanation.surface: A thespian keeps his spouse in a particular kind of home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actor' suggests the stage, but it means anyone who acts. 'keeps' puts W inside DOER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dower house is a smaller home on an estate for the widow of the late owner.

clue.text: Cordial man who refuses to strike head off gangsters

parts.note: a rat is a worker who breaks a strike or refuses to join it

indicators.note: head off says the gangsters lose their first letter

parts.note: the Mafia is a criminal gang organisation

explanation.surface: A friendly strikebreaker scares off the gang's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like an adjective, but here it is the noun, a drink. 'head off' cuts MAFIA to AFIA.
explanation.definitionFit: This almond-flavoured liqueur is a sweet drink, a sense of cordial.

clue.text: During brief diplomatic move, notice solemn music

indicators.note: During says the notice comes within the shortened diplomatic move
brief says the diplomatic move loses its last letter

parts.note: a demarche is a formal diplomatic step or protest
an ad is a notice in a newspaper

explanation.surface: An advertisement appears in the middle of a short diplomatic initiative, as sombre music plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' leaves DEMARCH, and 'During' sets the notice in the middle of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow, grave music played at a funeral procession is this kind of march.

clue.text: Policeman's sulky look, arresting one by the book

indicators.note: arresting says the sulky look holds the following pieces captive inside

parts.note: a moue is a pout, a sulky look
NT is the New Testament, part of the Bible, the book
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cop pulls a sour face while arresting someone strictly by the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the book' suggests following rules, but 'the book' is the Bible, and its New Testament is the abbreviation wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police is a police officer.

clue.text: Concerned with the main period after the start of spring, perhaps

indicators.note: after says the period comes later, following the start of spring

parts.note: Mar I, the first of March, can be taken as the first day of spring
a time is a period

explanation.surface: Something about the main season of the year, following early spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the sea, an old poetic sense. MAR I is 1 March, the start of meteorological spring, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything to do with the sea or seafaring is described this way, and the main is a poetic name for the ocean.

clue.text: Impostor clasps boss briefly in embrace

indicators.note: in says the shortened boss is placed inside the embrace

parts.note: a hug is an embrace

indicators.note: briefly says the word for boss loses its last letter

parts.note: an umbo is the raised central boss of a shield

explanation.surface: A fraud wraps the boss in a quick hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' looks like a manager, but it is the raised knob at the centre of a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A humbug is a fraud or sham, someone who pretends to be what they are not.

clue.text: Lake surrounds small wood

indicators.note: surrounds says the lake holds the small piece inside

parts.note: Bala Lake, in north Wales, is the largest natural lake in Wales

explanation.surface: A lake encircles a little wood.
explanation.walkthrough: BALA is a lake in north Wales. 'surrounds' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This very light timber from a tropical American tree is used for model making.

clue.text: Stretch of road, note, not included by AA

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Stretch of road, note, not included by AA' (4): MI is the note, but no reading found of 'not included by AA' giving LE, and searches turned up no parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Stretch of road, note, not included by AA

clue.text: Feeling of devastated figure missing out on university?

indicators.note: devastated says the remaining letters are wrecked and rearranged
missing out on says a letter is dropped from the word figure

explanation.surface: A distraught figure who failed to get a place at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing out on' drops U from FIGURE to leave FIGRE; 'devastated' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep sorrow, especially after a death, is a feeling.

clue.text: Cultivator of error said to be flash

indicators.note: said tells us the phrase is heard rather than read, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: one who tills sin: a sin tiller

explanation.surface: Someone who breeds wrongdoing is described as gaudy.
explanation.walkthrough: A tiller is one who cultivates, and sin is error, so a 'sin tiller' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny spark or trace is what the Latin word for it describes, a mere glimmer.

clue.text: Being on horse, fly — or flee

indicators.note: Being on says the fly sits on the horse, inside the seat that stands for it

parts.note: being in the saddle is being on horseback, so the saddle stands for the horse
a ked is a wingless fly that lives on sheep and other animals

explanation.surface: A rider urges a horse to bolt so as to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like a verb meaning flee, but it is the insect; being in the saddle is an idiom for riding.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away hurriedly is to scarper or bolt.

clue.text: Welshman contemplates navel, somewhat laid back

indicators.note: laid back says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Welsh chap, rather relaxed, gazes at his belly button.
explanation.walkthrough: SNAVE runs across 'contemplates navel'; 'laid back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Welsh surname stands for a man from Wales.
